title: Oncall Program Health Dashboard and Runbook Retirement Policy
author: Aisha Malik
content:
Overview:

This page defines the Oncall Program Health Dashboard and the formal Runbook Retirement Policy for Redwood Inference. It describes the metrics we track to assess oncall program health, the dashboard views, the measurable retirement criteria for runbooks, the retirement workflow (including handoffs and comms), and how runbook lifecycle ties into rotations, game days, postmortems, and customer-facing status messages.

Purpose:
- Maintain a sustainable oncall program with measurable signals for responder load, runbook efficacy, and incident resolution quality.
- Keep the runbook library lean, accurate, and discoverable so operators can resolve incidents quickly with minimal context switching.
- Provide a clear, repeatable process to retire stale/duplicate/inaccurate runbooks while preserving evidence for audits and postmortem learning.

Scope:
Applies to all runbooks, playbooks, and bridge/operator checklists in sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response and any service-specific runbooks that reference that library.

Program health metrics (definitions and targets):
1) Mean Time To Acknowledge (MTTA) — target: <= 5 minutes for P0, <= 15 minutes for P1.
2) Mean Time To Restore (MTTR) — target: <= 30 minutes for P0, <= 2 hours for P1.
3) Runbook Coverage (%) — percent of top-20 incident signatures that have a canonical runbook: target >= 95%.
4) Runbook Age (median days since last verification) — target <= 180 days.
5) Runbook Run Frequency — number of times a runbook has been executed in the last 12 months (live or in drills).
6) Postmortem Quality Gate Pass Rate — percent of postmortems passing peer review checklist: target >= 90%.
7) Oncall Burnout Index — composite metric (shift length violations, weekly pager load, survey sentiment): target maintain within healthy baseline; action if > 1.2x historical.

Dashboard views (minimum):
- Executive Summary: MTTA, MTTR, top impacted services, open P0s, 30/90-day trend for MTTR.
- Runbook Health: coverage %, median age, last verification date histogram, run frequency.
- Rotation Load: active pagers per shift, weekly pager counts per person, overtime hours.
- Drill & Game Day Outcomes: success/failure rate, average time to complete scenario, follow-up actions.
- Postmortem Intake: number of postmortems pending review, action items overdue.

Sample dashboard table (Runbook Health):
| Runbook ID | Owner | Last Verified | Runs (12m) | Status | Retirement Flag |
|------------|-------|---------------|-----------:|--------|-----------------|
| rb-cache-evict-001 | eng-serving-runtime | 2026-01-22 | 8 | active | no |
| rb-model-fallback-002 | eng-platform | 2025-08-05 | 1 | needs-verification | candidate |
| rb-oncall-handoff-003 | eng-sre | 2024-07-12 | 0 | deprecated | retired |

Runbook retirement criteria (a runbook becomes a "candidate for retirement" when ALL of the following are true):
1) No successful live runs in 12 months OR the run frequency is below the low-usage threshold (<= 1 run / 12 months).
2) Not referenced by an active service configuration or automation pipeline (verify with infra ownership and CI links).
3) Last verification > 180 days and owner cannot commit to an update within the next quarter.
4) Content is duplicate or superseded by another canonical runbook (explicit aliasing required).
5) No open postmortem or regulatory audit requirement that references the runbook.

Runbook retirement workflow (roles & steps):
- Roles:
  - Runbook Owner: primary author/maintainer (team listed in runbook metadata).
  - Runbook Steward: oncall-and-incident-response guild member assigned to ~30 runbooks for quarterly checks.
  - Approver: Service Owner or Eng Lead with authority to archive operational artifacts.

- Retirement steps (numbered):
  1) Trigger: Runbook flagged by dashboard (monthly flagging job) or nominated at quarterly Ops triage.
  2) Steward Review: Runbook Steward performs automated checks (links, CI references, telemetry).
  3) Owner Notification: Steward opens a retirement ticket (label: runbook-retire) and notifies owner with 14-day review window.
  4) Stakeholder Check: Owner confirms whether runbook should be updated, consolidated, or retired. If update requested, owner must supply verification date and plan within 14 days.
  5) Approver Decision: If no objection or owner confirms retirement, Approver signs off in ticket and assigns an archival date (default: 7 days after approval).
  6) Archive & Replace: Move runbook to /archive/runbooks/YYYY-MM and add a stub with pointer to replacement or reason for retention. Update dashboard metadata (status=retired).
  7) Evidence Pack: On archive, capture snapshot: runbook content, last run evidence, related incidents, and any regulatory notes; store in the evidence bucket with a retention tag.
  8) Notification: Publish a runbook-retirement digest to #oncall-ops and send a summary to product/security if impacted.

Fallback and rollback for mistaken retirements:
- If a retired runbook is needed during an incident, responders may promote the archived runbook back to active state with an emergency verification label. The promoting team must complete a post-restore verification within 48 hours and add the run frequency and evidence to the runbook history.

Integration with rotations and game days:
- Runbooks must be exercised in at least one game day per calendar year. Game day outcomes update the Runbook Health metrics automatically.
- New responders (shadow-to-solo progression) must complete execution of 5 canonical runbooks in shadow mode before solo shifts are assigned. The Runbook Steward validates completion.
- Rotation schedules must include a quarterly runbook review slot (30–60 minutes) for owners to confirm verification and update playbooks.

Postmortems and quality gate (how retirement interacts with incident learning):
- Every P0/P1 incident requires a postmortem within 7 business days. Postmortems must reference any runbooks used. If a runbook was followed but failed to resolve the incident, it cannot be retired until postmortem actions are closed or mitigated.
- Postmortem quality checklist (peer review pass required):
  - Clear incident timeline (UTC timestamps) and list of signals correlated.
  - Root cause analysis with evidence (logs, traces, KV-cache metrics).
  - Actions with owners and due dates (no more than 30 days for critical action items).
  - Link to runbook(s) executed and explicit assessment of runbook accuracy.

Customer-facing status and comms templates (use these when runbook retirement affects customer-facing behavior or when retiring automation that alters routing):
- Status page short template (for incident channel update):
  - Title: [SERVICE] Degraded performance — mitigation in progress
  - Body: We are investigating increased latency affecting [subset of customers/regions]. Our responders have applied a mitigation (automatic fallback) and are monitoring. Customers may see increased response times up to ~X seconds. We will provide updates every 30 minutes.
  - Impact: partial (region-specific) / degraded throughput / increased latency
  - Next update: <time UTC>
- Customer escalation email template (for enterprise customers):
  Subject: Incident update — [SERVICE] Degradation impacting <customer-name>
  Body:
  Hello <customer-contact>,

  We wanted to inform you that we identified increased latency for requests routed to <region/model-pool> starting at <time UTC>. Our oncall team applied a tactical mitigation and restored partial throughput at <time UTC>. We are currently validating the fix and expect full restoration by <ETA UTC>.

  What we did: <short bullets of mitigation steps>
  What we are doing next: <investigation, postmortem timeline, escalations>
  Impact to you: <specifics — request failures, delays, billing & credits if applicable>

  Owner: <oncall lead contact info>
  We will follow up with a full postmortem within 7 business days.

Automation and metadata requirements for runbooks (minimum):
- Every runbook must include front-matter fields (as tags or YAML block) that are machine-readable: runbook_id, owner_team, primary_owner, last_verified, severity_tags (P0/P1/P2), affected_services, ci_links, archive_status.
- The retirement job uses these fields to determine candidates automatically.
- Runbooks should include the command snippets and CLI invocations used by responders; these must be kept current and tested in the runbook verification steps.

Quarterly governance cycle (cadence):
1) Month 1: Dashboard refresh and steward flags; runbook owners notified.
2) Month 2: Runbook owners perform verifications and update run frequency logs. Game day schedule set.
3) Month 3: Ops triage meeting — approve retirements, consolidate duplicates, and publish the runbook-retire digest.

Evidence retention and audit considerations:
- Archived runbooks and their evidence pack are retained for 3 years (default) to satisfy incident evidence and regulatory requests.
- For enterprise customers with higher retention contracts, tag evidence packs with customer-specific retention policies.

Appendix A — Runbook retirement checklist (copyable):
- [ ] Confirm run frequency <= 1/12 months OR no runs in 12 months
- [ ] Confirm not referenced by CI/CD or automation (list CI links)
- [ ] Check postmortem links and regulatory artifacts; none open
- [ ] Owner has been notified and responded or timed out
- [ ] Approver sign-off obtained and archival date scheduled
- [ ] Evidence pack created and uploaded to evidence bucket
- [ ] Slack digest posted to #oncall-ops and stakeholders notified

Appendix B — Emergency restore template (use when a retired runbook must be promoted during an incident):
- Action: Restore runbook to active with label "emergency-restore"
- Required fields: restorer_name, restoration_time_UTC, incident_id, temporary_owner, verification_due (48h)
- Post-incident: Complete runbook verification and add lessons learned to postmortem

Appendix C — Example CLI snippet for archiving (for runbook owners):
```bash
# create archive folder and snapshot runbook
runbook-cli snapshot --id rb-<id> --output s3://redwood-evidence/runbooks/$(date +%Y-%m) --tag retired
runbook-cli set-status --id rb-<id> --status retired --archived_at $(date -I)
```
